compare.title: UScale vs Remini, BlurBuster and EnhanceFox — the same photo in four apps
compare.description: The same two photos run through UScale, Remini, BlurBuster and EnhanceFox. Full-size results, side-by-side close-ups and what each AI photo enhancer got right and wrong.
compare.h1: The same photo, four AI enhancers
compare.lead: We picked two hard files — a rainy night frame and a low-resolution video still — and ran each one through UScale, Remini, BlurBuster and EnhanceFox. One pass per app, nothing retouched afterwards.
compare.method_p: Both files went into every app at their original size and came straight back out. UScale ran in Creative Upscale mode. The competitor exports of the park photo returned mirrored, so we flipped them back to match the original — nothing else was touched. Every result is shown at the same display size, which is how you would look at them on a phone. Tested in August 2026 on the App Store versions current at the time.
compare.alt_before: The original photo before any AI enhancement
compare.table_note: Everything in this table comes from the two runs above, with UScale in Creative Upscale mode. UScale also has an on-device mode: it is a smaller jump than Creative Upscale, but on files like these it still resolves more real detail than the three rivals — without the photo leaving your iPhone.
compare.disclaimer: Remini, BlurBuster and EnhanceFox are trademarks of their respective owners and are not affiliated with UScale. This page shows one test on two files, run in August 2026. Apps change, modes differ, and your own photos will behave differently — the source files are the ones you see above, so the test is easy to repeat.

tests.h2: Test 1 — a rainy night frame with no human face
tests.sub: 823 × 460, compressed, neon behind rain — and no human face in the frame.
tests.look: The web lines on the mask, the droplets on the shoulders, and the rain falling in front of the lens.

tests.h2: Test 2 — a low-resolution video still with two faces
tests.sub: 840 × 560, soft and flat, grabbed from a video. This is the case every photo enhancer is built for.
tests.look: The eyes, single hairs, the print on the dress and the blades of grass.

compare.modes_p: BlurBuster's result depends on which mode you tap, and the difference is not subtle. Its other pass on the same night frame came back bigger — 3296 × 1840 instead of 1646 × 920 — and clearly worse: waxy fabric, smeared rain, mushy edges. Finding the mode that actually helps is left to you.

uscale.verdict: Adds detail without moving the picture: same colours, same framing, texture that belongs to the photo. The on-device mode keeps the file on your iPhone.

remini.verdict: Best of the three rivals on human faces, close to a no-op when the frame has none. Expect a rebuilt face on a background that is still soft.

blurbuster.verdict: Makes the boldest-looking picture and the least faithful one. Colour, contrast and texture all move, and the mode picker decides how far.

enhancefox.verdict: The safest of the three and the least ambitious: more pixels, a little more edge contrast, not much new detail.

rest.remini: Left as soft as the source

faq.q: Which app won?
faq.a: On these two files, UScale. On the park photo Remini's faces are genuinely competitive, but the dress, the grass and the trees stay as soft as the source — and on the night frame Remini changed almost nothing. BlurBuster produces the most dramatic picture and the least faithful one, and EnhanceFox mostly adds pixels.

faq.q: Which UScale mode was used?
faq.a: Creative Upscale — UScale's cloud mode, the one that adds the most detail. UScale can also enhance entirely on your iPhone: that mode is a smaller jump than Creative Upscale, but on files like these it still recovers more real detail than the three rivals, and the photo never leaves the device.

faq.q: Why did Remini do so little to the Spider-Man frame?
faq.a: Remini's strength is a face model, and a mask is not a face. With nothing to rebuild, the picture comes back close to the way it went in. It is the same reason Remini shines on old portraits and stalls on landscapes, pets, artwork and screenshots.

faq.q: Why are all the outputs different sizes?
faq.a: Each app decides its own output resolution — 2× in BlurBuster and EnhanceFox, roughly 4× in Remini, close to 6× in UScale. Bigger is not automatically better: BlurBuster's larger mode returned the biggest file of the night-frame test and the worst-looking one.

faq.q: Is this a fair test?
faq.a: It is one test on two files, so treat it as a starting point — and check it for yourself. Both source photos are right here: run them through the free tier of any of these apps and compare what comes back. Every app here got the same original at full size and a single standard pass, and no result was retouched afterwards. What it does not cover is every mode, every subscription tier and every kind of photo.

faq.q: Are these the current versions of the apps?
faq.a: The runs were done in August 2026 with the versions on the App Store at that time. Apps update often; if you get a clearly different result on the same kind of photo, send it to us and we will re-run the comparison.

unblur-photo-iphone.h1: How to unblur a photo on your iPhone
unblur-photo-iphone.answer: To unblur a photo on iPhone, open UScale, tap Upscale your media → Photos and pick the blurry shot, then choose Creative Upscale. It reconstructs edges, texture and facial detail instead of merely sharpening them, and returns a clean 2K, 4K or 8K copy in about 30 seconds.
unblur-photo-iphone.supply: A blurry photo in your iPhone photo library
unblur-photo-iphone.intro: Sharpening and unblurring are different jobs. Sharpening lifts contrast around edges that already exist; AI unblurring infers what the missing detail looked like and rebuilds it. UScale gives you three ways to do that, and the mode matters more than any setting inside it. Creative Upscale rebuilds the most detail but runs in the cloud; Face Enhancer and Regular Upscale run on your iPhone and upload nothing.
unblur-photo-iphone.why_h: Why your photo came out blurry
unblur-photo-iphone.why_p: Which kind of blur you are dealing with decides how much you can realistically recover.
why_list: Low resolution — a cropped, screenshotted or messaging-app photo. The easiest case, and what Creative Upscale handles best.
Heavy compression — a file re-saved and re-shared many times. Denoise and upscale run in the same pass and usually clean it up.
Missed focus — the camera locked onto the background. Recoverable while the subject still has some definition left.
Camera shake — mild shake cleans up nicely; a long, obvious smear does not.
Motion blur — the honest weak spot: the smear runs in one direction and today's models rebuild it poorly. A model built for motion blur is in testing now.
unblur-photo-iphone.steps_h: Unblur a photo in UScale, step by step
unblur-photo-iphone.steps_intro: Under a minute end to end. Start with Creative Upscale — it gives the best result on most blurry photos.

steps.p: On the UScale home screen tap Upscale your media, choose Photos and select the blurry shot. Several photos can go in one batch, and there is no account to create.
It reconstructs texture and fills in detail the file no longer holds, rather than only sharpening what is there. It runs on our servers, so this photo is uploaded.
The only setting Creative Upscale needs. 2K is plenty for sharing, 4K is the safe default, 8K is for printing or cropping hard into the result.

steps.h: Tap Upscale and give it about 30 seconds
steps.p: Pinch to zoom into hair, fabric weave and text — that is where you see whether real detail came back or contrast was merely added.

steps.h: Want it fully private? Use Face Enhancer or Regular Upscale
steps.p: Both run on your device and work in airplane mode. They ask for a style instead of a resolution: Natural keeps the original texture, Smoothed gives cleaner, harder edges. Either way the sharp copy is saved as a new photo and the original stays untouched.

tips: Start from the original file, not a screenshot or a copy that has been through a messaging app. Every re-save throws away detail the AI would have used.
Crop before you enhance, so the model spends its resolution on the part of the picture you care about.
On the on-device modes, try Natural and Smoothed on the same photo — it takes seconds and the difference is obvious.
Motion blur is the hardest case for every AI enhancer. Expect an improvement rather than a rescue.
For a photo that is both dark and blurry, brighten it first and enhance second.
Still not happy? Email the photo to alexandr.graschenkov91@gmail.com — the developer answers personally.
unblur-photo-iphone.cta_p: Free for two photos a day, no account, and the on-device modes never upload a thing.

faq.q: Which mode should I use — Creative Upscale, Face Enhancer or Regular Upscale?
faq.a: Creative Upscale gives the best result on most blurry photos because it can rebuild detail the file no longer contains, but it processes in the cloud. If you would rather nothing left your iPhone, use Face Enhancer for people and Regular Upscale for everything else.

faq.q: Can AI fix motion blur?
faq.a: Only partly. Motion blur smears detail along the direction of movement, leaving no clean structure to anchor to. A model built specifically for motion blur is being tested and will be added to the app.

faq.q: Can AI unblur a photo that is completely smeared?
faq.a: No. With no recognisable structure left the model invents detail that was never there. AI unblurring works best on mild to moderate blur, where edges are soft but still present.

faq.q: Does unblurring a photo need an internet connection?
faq.a: Only for Creative Upscale. Face Enhancer and Regular Upscale process the photo on your iPhone, so they work in airplane mode and upload nothing.

restore-old-photos.description: Restore old family photos on your phone: how to photograph a print, which AI restoration mode to pick, and how to repair scratches, folds and fading.
restore-old-photos.h1: How to restore old photos with your phone
restore-old-photos.answer: To restore an old photo, photograph the print flat in soft daylight, then open UScale, tap Upscale your media → Photos and pick the shot. Choose Photo restoration, set the mode — Enhanced Colorize suits most prints — and tap Upscale. The repaired photo comes back in about 40 seconds.
restore-old-photos.supply: A printed photo and an iPhone camera or scanner
restore-old-photos.intro: Most old-photo restorations are lost at the capture stage: a shadow across the print, a glare spot from a ceiling light or a slightly skewed angle costs more detail than the AI can put back. Spend two minutes on the capture and the rest is one mode choice and one tap. Restoration runs on our servers rather than on your iPhone, so it uploads the photo and needs a connection.
restore-old-photos.why_h: What actually goes wrong with old prints
restore-old-photos.why_p: Different damage needs a different mode, so it helps to know what you are looking at.
why_list: Scratches and dust from handling and storage — the easiest damage to remove automatically.
Folds and cracks where the print was bent, often running straight through a face.
Fading and colour shift — 1970s and 1980s colour prints drift towards orange or magenta as the dyes break down.
Tears and missing corners, which have to be rebuilt rather than cleaned: that is what Advanced Fix is for.
Softness from the original camera and film, which is a resolution problem rather than damage.
restore-old-photos.steps_h: Restore an old photo in UScale, step by step
restore-old-photos.steps_intro: Do the capture properly, then it is four taps and about 40 seconds of waiting.

steps.h: Photograph the print flat and evenly lit
steps.p: Lay the print near a window, out of direct sun, and hold the phone parallel to it so the edges stay rectangular. Never use the flash — it leaves a glare spot no model can remove.
Trim away the table, the border and any white margin, so the AI works on the picture rather than on the surface under it.

steps.h: Open Upscale your media → Photos and choose Photo restoration
steps.p: Select the shot — or several, to restore a box of similar snapshots with the same settings. The Cloud Processing badge marks Photo restoration as a server-side mode.
Tap the mode card for Restore, Restore & Colorize, Enhanced Colorize and Advanced Fix. Enhanced Colorize is the one to start with; the section below covers the rest.

steps.h: Set the advanced options if you need them
steps.p: All three are optional: Negative for film negatives, Increased resolution for more fine detail, and Prompt for facts the model cannot guess, such as eye colour or the colour of a dress.

steps.h: Tap Upscale, then save or re-run
steps.p: The result arrives in about 40 seconds. Zoom into faces, hair and fabric to see whether the damage was repaired or merely blurred over, then save the copy — the original scan is untouched — or run it again in another mode.

restore-old-photos.modes_intro: Photo restoration opens with a Mode picker. These are the app's own previews — one damaged portrait through each mode.

restore-old-photos.options_h: Advanced options: Negative, Increased resolution and Prompt
restore-old-photos.options_intro: Under the mode picker sit three optional settings, each solving a specific problem.

options.sub: Add eye color, clothing color, or other important details
options.p: Free text for what the model cannot infer — “blue eyes”, “red dress”, “green army uniform”. Ask whoever remembers the photo. Not used by Advanced Fix.

options.p: Server models that recover more fine detail, at the cost of predictability: they can add detail the print never had.

options.p: For film negatives rather than prints: the frame is inverted and the orange film mask neutralised before restoration runs.

tips: Soft, indirect daylight beats any lamp — an overcast day by a window is the ideal light for copying prints.
If the print is glossy, tilt the print rather than the phone until the reflection slides off the image.
Try two modes before deciding. Enhanced Colorize against Restore & Colorize takes a minute, and the difference on faces is obvious.
Fill in the Prompt for anything you actually know: “blue eyes, dark green uniform” fixes what colourisation gets wrong most often.
Restore a box of similar snapshots as one batch, and keep the untouched scan as well as the result — future models will do more with it.
Stuck on a particular print? Email it to alexandr.graschenkov91@gmail.com — the developer answers personally.
restore-old-photos.cta_p: Restore, colorize and reprint the photos in the shoebox. Restoration runs on our cloud models and is part of Premium — the annual plan starts with a {trial_days}-day free trial.

faq.q: Which restoration mode should I use?
faq.a: Enhanced Colorize on most old prints — it repairs, colorizes and sharpens in one pass. Restore & Colorize when that sharpening overreaches on a soft scan, Restore when the colours should stay as they are, and Advanced Fix only for severe damage.

faq.q: How long does restoration take?
faq.a: About 40 seconds per photo. The work happens on our servers, so your connection and the queue matter, and a batch takes proportionally longer.

faq.q: Do I need a scanner, or is a phone camera enough?
faq.a: A modern phone camera is enough for almost every print, as long as the lighting is even and the phone is parallel to the photo. A flatbed scanner is only clearly better for very small prints and for negatives.

faq.q: Are my old photos uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: Yes — restoration is the cloud part of UScale. The photo goes to our processing provider, stays available for download for a limited time and is then deleted. On-device tools such as Face Enhancer never upload anything.

faq.q: Can AI repair a photo with a piece torn off?
faq.a: Advanced Fix can rebuild a missing corner or a tear across a background convincingly. A missing face is different — the model will invent one, and it will not be the person you remember.

faq.q: Will restoration change how people look?
faq.a: Mildly, yes. Restoration reconstructs detail rather than recovering it, and Advanced Fix moves furthest from the original, so compare every result against the scan before you save it.

colorize-black-and-white-photos.description: Colorize black and white photos on your phone with AI: which restoration mode gives the most natural colour, and how to steer tones with a prompt.
colorize-black-and-white-photos.h1: How to colorize black and white photos
colorize-black-and-white-photos.answer: To colorize a black and white photo, open UScale, tap Upscale your media → Photos and pick the photo, then choose Photo restoration. Set the mode to Enhanced Colorize and tap Upscale. Colour arrives in about 40 seconds, and a prompt such as “blue eyes, red dress” steers it towards the real thing.
colorize-black-and-white-photos.supply: A black and white photo, scanned or photographed
colorize-black-and-white-photos.intro: Colourisation is informed guessing. The model has learned that grass is green and that skin sits within a narrow range of tones, but it cannot know your grandmother's coat was red rather than brown — which is what the Prompt field is for. One thing to know before you start: colourising is not a separate button in UScale. It is a mode inside Photo restoration, so the same pass that adds the colour also removes the scratches.
colorize-black-and-white-photos.why_h: What makes a colourisation look convincing
colorize-black-and-white-photos.why_p: Some photos colourise almost perfectly and others look painted. The difference usually comes down to these factors.
why_list: Contrast range — a print with real blacks and whites gives the model far more to work with than a flat, grey scan.
Recognisable content — faces, skies, grass, wood and common clothing colourise reliably because they appear constantly in training data.
Capture quality — a shadow or a glare spot across the print is read as part of the scene and coloured in as if it belonged there.
Resolution — a small, soft scan produces muddy colour patches, which is where Enhanced Colorize earns its place.
Unusual objects — a uniform, a painted sign or a specific dress is where colourisation guesses wrong, and where a prompt fixes it.
colorize-black-and-white-photos.steps_h: Colorize a photo in UScale, step by step
colorize-black-and-white-photos.steps_intro: Repair and colour happen in the same pass, so this is one job rather than two.

steps.p: Photograph it flat in soft daylight, without flash, and crop to the image area. A shadow across a face becomes a grey patch that the model then tries to colour.
Tap Upscale your media on the home screen, choose Photos and select the picture. Several photos can go in at once and share the same settings.
Colorize lives inside Photo restoration rather than as a separate tool, and the Cloud Processing badge is the reminder that it runs on our servers.

steps.h: Set the mode to Enhanced Colorize
steps.p: Two of the four modes add colour. Enhanced Colorize is the stronger one and the right default; Restore & Colorize is the gentler alternative.

steps.h: Add a prompt if you know the real colours
steps.p: Open Prompt in Advanced options and type what you know: “blue eyes, navy jacket, red brick house”. It is the single biggest improvement available, because it replaces guesswork with fact.

steps.h: Tap Upscale, then save both versions
steps.p: Colour arrives in about 40 seconds. Zoom into the faces first — grey or waxy skin means it is worth re-running with a prompt or the other colorize mode. The colour version saves as a new photo and the monochrome original stays where it was.

colorize-black-and-white-photos.modes_intro: Two of the four restoration modes add colour, one deliberately does not, and one is reserved for wrecked prints.

modes.p: The best colourisation in the app and the one to start with. It repairs, colours and rebuilds detail in one pass, so skin and fabric hold texture.

modes.p: The same repair and colour without the sharpening. Switch to it when Enhanced Colorize looks synthetic on a small or soft scan.

modes.img_alt: Restore mode preview in UScale — an old portrait cleaned up and left in black and white

modes.p: A heavier model for cracked, torn or badly stained prints. It rebuilds aggressively and ignores the Prompt field.

colorize-black-and-white-photos.options_h: Steering the colours: Prompt and the other advanced options
colorize-black-and-white-photos.options_intro: Colourisation is the one place where these options change the result dramatically rather than subtly.

options.sub: Add eye color, clothing color, or other important details
options.p: Type the colours you know — “green eyes, yellow summer dress, blue sky”. The model follows it, turning a plausible guess into the right answer.

options.sub: Generates the result at a higher resolution
options.p: Server models that hold more fine detail, useful if you plan to print. They are less predictable, so compare against a run with it off.

options.sub: Invert and normalize photo colors before restoration
options.p: Only for film negatives: it inverts and normalises the frame before the colour pass runs.

colorize-black-and-white-photos.img_alt: A black and white family photo colorized with AI in UScale on iPhone
colorize-black-and-white-photos.img_caption: The same 1950s portrait, restored and then colorized.
tips: Photos taken outdoors in daylight colourise best. Indoor shots lit by one lamp give weaker cues, so the prompt matters more there.
Judge the result by the faces. If skin tones read grey or waxy, nothing else in the picture will convince either.
If a large area comes out an odd colour, name it in the prompt — “brown wooden door”, “grey stone wall”.
Show the result to someone who was there; they often remember the real colour of a dress or a wall.
Never overwrite the monochrome original. It is the historical document; the colour version is an interpretation of it.
colorize-black-and-white-photos.cta_p: Colorize, repair and upscale old prints on your iPhone. Restoration uses our cloud models and is part of Premium, starting with a {trial_days}-day free trial.

faq.q: Where is the Colorize button in UScale?
faq.a: There is no separate Colorize tool. Tap Upscale your media → Photos, choose Photo restoration, and set the Mode to Enhanced Colorize or Restore & Colorize. The same pass repairs the print and adds the colour.

faq.q: Enhanced Colorize or Restore & Colorize — what is the difference?
faq.a: Both repair and colourise. Enhanced Colorize also rebuilds fine detail, so it looks sharper and suits most photos. Restore & Colorize leaves the underlying quality alone, which is safer on very small or soft scans.

faq.q: Are the colours historically accurate?
faq.a: They are plausible, not documented. Skin, sky and vegetation are usually right; clothing and painted objects are educated guesses. Use the Prompt field to supply the colours you know.

faq.q: Can I colorize a photo that is already partly colour?
faq.a: A faded colour print is better served by the plain Restore mode, which removes the damage and keeps the existing palette, than by a colorize mode built for genuinely monochrome sources.

faq.q: Does colourising need an internet connection?
faq.a: Yes. Restoration and colourisation run on our servers because the models are too heavy for a phone, so the photo is uploaded and the result comes back in about 40 seconds. UScale's on-device tools work offline.

upscale-image-4k.card_title: How to upscale an image to 4K
upscale-image-4k.card_desc: Turn a small, low-resolution picture into a print-ready file.
upscale-image-4k.title: How to Upscale an Image to 4K on iPhone
upscale-image-4k.description: Upscale an image to 4K on iPhone. How AI upscaling differs from resizing, and how Creative Upscale turns a low-res picture into a sharp 4K or 8K file.
upscale-image-4k.h1: How to upscale an image to 4K
upscale-image-4k.answer: To upscale an image to 4K, open UScale, tap Upscale your media → Photos, select the picture and choose Creative Upscale, then set the output to 4K. The AI reconstructs edges and texture instead of stretching pixels, so the enlarged file is genuinely sharper, not just bigger.
upscale-image-4k.supply: A low-resolution image in your photo library
upscale-image-4k.intro: Resizing and upscaling are not the same operation. Resizing spreads the pixels you already have over a bigger canvas, which is why an enlargement goes soft. AI upscaling generates new pixels from what the model has learned about edges, skin, fabric and text, so the result can hold more usable detail than the original file did. Creative Upscale is the mode built for this: you pick 2K, 4K or 8K and it rebuilds the detail to fill it. Regular Upscale and Face Enhancer stay closer to the source and run on your device.
upscale-image-4k.why_h: How much resolution can you actually gain?
upscale-image-4k.why_p: The realistic ceiling depends on what is in the source file, not just on its pixel count.
why_list: A clean, in-focus small photo upscales beautifully — the ideal case for a 4K or 8K output.
A screenshot of a photo has already lost data twice; expect a good result rather than a perfect one.
A heavily compressed image from a chat app needs denoising as well as upscaling, which happens in the same pass.
An out-of-focus original stays soft in outline — upscaling multiplies pixels, it does not re-focus the lens.
Text and logos upscale surprisingly well, because their shapes are highly predictable to the model.
upscale-image-4k.steps_h: Upscale to 4K in UScale, step by step
upscale-image-4k.steps_intro: Three taps to a 4K file, one more to save it.

steps.p: Tap Upscale your media on the home screen, choose Photos and select the image — or a whole set, processed as one batch. Use the original from your camera roll rather than a re-shared copy.

This is the mode to use when the goal is resolution. It reconstructs detail instead of interpolating it, which keeps a large enlargement looking like a photograph. Processing happens in the cloud, so the image is uploaded.
2K, 4K and 8K are absolute targets, so there are no multipliers to work out: 2K for sharing, 4K for prints and large screens, 8K when you intend to crop hard into the result.

steps.h: Tap Upscale and give it about 30 seconds
steps.p: Pinch to zoom right in when the result comes back. Edges, fabric and single blades of grass show whether detail was reconstructed or merely smoothed.

steps.h: Save it — or keep it on device with Regular Upscale
steps.p: The upscaled file saves as a new copy and the original stays at its original size. If you would rather nothing was uploaded, Regular Upscale and Face Enhancer run on your iPhone and ask for a Natural or Smoothed style instead of a target resolution.

upscale-image-4k.img_alt: A low-resolution photo of two children upscaled with the UScale AI image upscaler on iPhone
upscale-image-4k.img_caption: An 840-pixel-wide source upscaled with Creative Upscale — reconstructed detail, not stretched pixels.
upscale-image-4k.tips_h: Getting the most from an upscale
tips: Crop before you upscale, not after. The output resolution then goes entirely to the part of the picture you want.
For printing, aim for about 300 pixels per inch: a 4K-wide file prints cleanly at roughly 32 cm across.
Do not upscale twice. Running an upscale on an already-upscaled file compounds the model's guesses and looks waxy.
Visible JPEG blocking is a compression artefact — the enhance pass cleans it up before enlarging.
Batch mode is the fastest way to take a whole set of product or holiday shots to 4K at the same setting.
upscale-image-4k.cta_p: Two free enhancements a day, and Creative Upscale at 4K or 8K is one tap away in premium.

faq.q: Is 4x the same as 4K?
faq.a: No. 4x is a multiplier applied to your image's dimensions; 4K is an absolute width of about 3840 pixels. Creative Upscale asks for the absolute target — 2K, 4K or 8K — while Regular Upscale works in 2x and 4x multipliers.

faq.q: Does upscaling make the file much larger?
faq.a: Yes — a 4K file holds many times the pixel count of a phone-sized source, so expect a much bigger file. That is what makes the result printable.

faq.q: Can I upscale an image without an internet connection?
faq.a: Yes, with Regular Upscale or Face Enhancer, which run on your device and work in airplane mode. Creative Upscale rebuilds detail far more aggressively and processes in the cloud, so it needs a connection.

enhance-video-quality.card_title: How to improve video quality on iPhone
enhance-video-quality.card_desc: Upscale a clip 2x or 4x on-device, in a style that suits the footage.
enhance-video-quality.title: How to Improve Video Quality on iPhone with AI (2026)
enhance-video-quality.description: Improve video quality on iPhone: upscale a clip 2x or 4x, clean up grain and compression, and pick the upscale style that suits your footage — all on-device in UScale.
enhance-video-quality.h1: How to improve video quality on iPhone
enhance-video-quality.answer: To improve video quality on iPhone, open UScale, tap Upscale your media → Videos and pick the clip. Choose Upscale Video — or Enhance Animation for cartoons and 3D — set the scale to 2x or 4x, choose the Smoothed or Natural style, trim to the part you want and tap Upscale. Every frame is enhanced on your device and saved as a new video.
enhance-video-quality.supply: A video clip in your photo library
enhance-video-quality.intro: Video enhancement is photo enhancement repeated a few thousand times, which is why so few phone apps do it well. UScale runs the same on-device models frame by frame and keeps them consistent, so the result does not shimmer between frames. You choose the scale, the style and the section to process before it starts — and nothing is uploaded, so a long clip has nowhere to queue.
enhance-video-quality.why_p: It helps to know which problem you are actually fixing, because the same enhance pass addresses them to different degrees.
why_list: Low resolution — an older 720p or 480p clip on a modern screen looks soft simply because it is being stretched.
Compression — footage downloaded or re-shared repeatedly develops blocking and smearing around motion.
Sensor noise — anything filmed indoors or at night carries grain that gets worse as you brighten it.
Analogue transfer artefacts — VHS and camcorder captures carry interlacing lines and colour bleed.
Soft optics — old phone and camcorder lenses were never sharp to begin with; AI can only recover so much.
enhance-video-quality.steps_h: Enhance a video in UScale, step by step
enhance-video-quality.steps_intro: Everything below runs on your device — no upload, no queue, and it works in airplane mode.

steps.p: On the home screen tap Upscale your media, switch to Videos and pick the clip. Work from the original recording where you can — a copy that came through a messaging app has already been re-compressed.

steps.h: Choose Upscale Video or Enhance Animation
steps.p: Upscale Video is the general model for filmed footage. Enhance Animation is trained on drawn and rendered frames — use it for cartoons, anime and 3D graphics, where flat colour areas and clean line work need very different treatment from camera noise.

2x is the safe default for footage that is already reasonably sharp. 4x is for genuinely low-resolution sources you want to fill a large screen with; it multiplies the pixels, and the processing time, by four.

Smoothed gives more contrast along edges and irons out noise more aggressively. Natural holds on to the original texture, which suits detailed footage — though it can leave artefacts in blurred backgrounds. If you are unsure, run a few seconds each way.

steps.h: Trim to the part you want
steps.p: Most clips have a usable core and a lot of dead time. Set the section to enhance before you start: fewer frames means proportionally less processing and a smaller output file.

steps.h: Tap Upscale and leave the app open
steps.p: Processing time depends on the resolution, the scale you chose, how many frames you selected and how fast your device is. Keep UScale in the foreground — sending it to the background can stop the pass — and put the phone on a charger for anything long. Then play the result next to the original, watching motion and faces.

enhance-video-quality.modes_intro: The two video modes use different models. Picking the wrong one is the single most common reason a result looks off, so choose by what was in front of the camera — or whether there was a camera at all.

modes.sub: Camera recordings of the real world
modes.p: Handles the things real sensors produce: grain, compression blocking, motion blur and soft optics. This is what you want for phone clips, camcorder transfers, drone shots and anything filmed.

Drawn and rendered frames have no sensor noise — they have flat colour fields, hard outlines and clean gradients, and a photo model tends to soften exactly those. Enhance Animation keeps the line work crisp and the colour areas clean.

enhance-video-quality.options_intro: Two settings shape the output, and both are visible before you start the pass: how far the frames are enlarged, and how the model treats detail on the way there.

options.p: Enough for most footage, and the fastest to process. A 1080p clip lands at 4K, which is more than any social platform will keep after it re-compresses your upload.
For genuinely low-resolution sources — old 480p or 720p clips — that need to fill a large screen. Four times the pixels means roughly four times the work, so trim tightly before you run it.
Pushes edges harder and smooths more aggressively, which suppresses grain and compression noise. The safer choice for noisy, dark or heavily compressed footage, at the cost of some fine texture.

Preserves skin, fabric and foliage detail instead of ironing it flat — the better look when the source is clean. Watch defocused backgrounds, where it can bring out artefacts that the smoothed pass would have hidden.

enhance-video-quality.img_alt: Improving video quality on iPhone with UScale — before and after frames of an upscaled clip
enhance-video-quality.img_caption: A low-resolution clip upscaled frame by frame on-device.
enhance-video-quality.video_caption: A real before-and-after from the app: the same clip, upscaled with AI.
tips: Always work from the original recording. A clip you sent through a messaging app has been re-compressed and lost detail that no model can restore.
Keep the phone plugged in and the app on screen. Frame-by-frame AI is genuinely demanding, and a backgrounded app can lose the whole pass.
Test on the hardest few seconds first — the darkest, softest or busiest part of the clip. If a setting survives that, it will hold up across the rest.
If the footage is dark, enhancing it will also amplify the grain. Smoothed handles that better than Natural.
Use Enhance Animation for anything drawn or rendered, even a screen recording of a game — there is no camera noise in those frames for the photo model to work with.
For social media, 2x is usually enough: the platform re-compresses your upload anyway, so a huge 4x file mostly spends processing time you will not see.
enhance-video-quality.cta_p: Five free seconds of video every day, processed entirely on your iPhone.

faq.q: How long does it take to enhance a video?
faq.a: It depends on the clip's resolution, the scale you picked, how many frames you selected and how powerful your device is, because every frame is processed individually. A few trimmed seconds take about a minute on a recent iPhone; a long 4x pass takes considerably more.

faq.q: Smoothed or Natural — which style should I use?
faq.a: Smoothed for noisy, dark or heavily compressed footage: it gives more contrast along edges and cleans up more. Natural for clean, detailed sources, because it holds the original texture — though blurred backgrounds can pick up artefacts. Trim a few seconds and try both; it is quick.

faq.q: Can I upscale a video to 4K?
faq.a: Yes. A 1080p clip run at 2x lands at 4K, and 4x goes well beyond it. Whether it looks like true 4K depends on how much real detail the source had to begin with.

faq.q: What should I use for cartoons or 3D animation?
faq.a: Enhance Animation. It is built for frames that were drawn or rendered rather than filmed, so it keeps outlines sharp and flat colour areas clean instead of treating them as noise to be smoothed.

faq.q: Why did my video stop processing?
faq.a: Almost always because the app went to the background. Keep UScale in the foreground while it works, and leave the phone on a charger for long clips so it does not run flat mid-pass.

faq.q: Is my video uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Video enhancement runs entirely on your device, which is also why it keeps working in airplane mode.

slow-motion-video.card_title: How to make a video slow motion
slow-motion-video.card_desc: Raise a clip's frame rate with AI, then slow the moment down.
slow-motion-video.title: How to Make a Video Slow Motion on iPhone with AI (2026)
slow-motion-video.description: Turn a normal video into slow motion on iPhone: increase the frame rate 2x or 4x with AI frame interpolation, pick the moment to slow down, all on-device.
slow-motion-video.h1: How to make a video slow motion on iPhone
slow-motion-video.answer: To make a normal video slow motion on iPhone, open UScale, tap Upscale your media → Videos and pick the clip. Choose Slow Motion, set the output FPS to 2x or 4x and tap Increase FPS. When it finishes, mark the section you want slowed and save it as a new video.
slow-motion-video.supply: A video clip filmed at normal speed
slow-motion-video.intro: Slowing a clip down in a normal editor does not create slow motion — it creates a stutter. A 30 fps recording played at quarter speed still has only 30 frames to show you, each one held on screen four times as long. UScale fixes the cause instead: it generates the frames that were never filmed, doubling or quadrupling the frame rate, and only then do you choose which moment to slow down. All of it runs on your iPhone — nothing is uploaded.
slow-motion-video.why_h: Why AI slow motion looks different
slow-motion-video.why_p: Frame interpolation analyses the motion between two consecutive frames and synthesises the frames that would have existed in between.
why_list: Slowing footage down without new frames gives choppy playback — the stuttery slow-mo everyone recognises.
Frame blending, the older trick, cross-fades between frames and leaves ghosting around anything that moves.
AI interpolation tracks the motion and draws genuinely new frames, so movement stays crisp instead of smearing.
The Photos app can only slow clips you filmed in slo-mo mode at a high frame rate. UScale creates that frame rate afterwards, from ordinary footage.
So any clip qualifies, including recordings from years ago — jumps, pets, sport, water, reveals.
slow-motion-video.steps_h: Make a slow-motion clip in UScale, step by step
slow-motion-video.steps_intro: Everything below happens on your device — no upload, no queue, and it works in airplane mode.

steps.p: On the home screen tap Upscale your media, switch to Videos and pick the recording. Any normal-speed clip works; you do not need to have filmed in slo-mo mode.

Slow Motion is the frame-interpolation mode: rather than sharpening each frame, it adds frames between them. The line under the player shows the clip's current frame rate and the frame rate you will end up with.
2x doubles the frame rate, so 30 fps becomes 60. 4x quadruples it to 120 and buys a much deeper slow-down, at the cost of asking the model to invent three frames for every filmed one.

steps.h: Tap Increase FPS and leave the app open
steps.p: Processing time depends on the resolution, the number of frames and how fast your device is. Keep UScale in the foreground — sending it to the background can stop the pass and you start over — and put the phone on a charger for anything long.

steps.h: Pick the moment to slow down
steps.p: With the extra frames in place, mark the section you want in slow motion, much as you would on a slo-mo clip in the Photos app. The rest of the video carries on at normal speed.

Play it back and watch the edges of moving objects — interpolation artefacts, when they appear, show up around hands, ball edges and splashing water. Save the result as a new video; the original clip is untouched.

slow-motion-video.options_h: Output FPS and the fast model
slow-motion-video.options_intro: By default the pass runs on the strongest frame-interpolation models that fit on the device, so quality is the starting point. Two settings change it: the multiplier on the Slow Motion screen, and the model choice in Settings.

options.p: One generated frame between every pair of real ones — the safest interpolation and the quickest to process. Enough for a natural, gentle slow-down of most footage.
Three generated frames for every filmed one, so the moment can be stretched much further and still play smoothly. It takes proportionally longer and asks more of the model on fast, erratic movement.

A lighter interpolation model that runs three to five times quicker. Worth switching on for long or high-resolution clips built from large shapes and broad motion; leave it off when fine detail — faces, hair, text, fabric — has to survive into the new frames.

slow-motion-video.img_alt: Creating AI slow motion from a normal video clip in UScale on iPhone
slow-motion-video.img_caption: UScale generating in-between frames to turn a normal clip into slow motion.
slow-motion-video.video_caption: AI slow motion generated on-device from a normal-speed recording.
tips: Keep the phone plugged in and the app on screen. Frame interpolation is genuinely demanding, and a backgrounded app can lose the whole pass.
Short beats long. One to three seconds of real time is where slow motion lands hardest, and fewer frames means far less processing.
Steady footage interpolates best — heavy camera shake gives the model conflicting motion cues.
Good light means a shorter exposure per frame, so less motion blur is baked into the source and the generated frames come out cleaner.
Avoid clips with a cut inside them. Interpolating across a scene change produces a strange morph between two unrelated shots.
If the source is low resolution, run the enhance pass first and the FPS increase after — there are fewer frames to upscale, and the interpolation then works from sharper ones.
slow-motion-video.cta_p: AI frame interpolation that runs on your iPhone, with five free seconds of video every day.

faq.q: Do I need to film in slo-mo mode first?
faq.a: No — that is the point. UScale generates the extra frames from a normal-speed recording, so a clip you filmed months ago can still become slow motion.

faq.q: How is this different from slowing a clip in the Photos app?
faq.a: Photos can only make slow motion out of footage that was already filmed at a high frame rate; slowing an ordinary clip there just stretches the frames you have, and playback stutters. UScale creates the missing frames first, then lets you pick the moment to slow down.

faq.q: Should I choose 2x or 4x?
faq.a: 2x for a natural slow-down and the fastest processing, 4x when you want the moment stretched much further. The frame rate you start from and the one you will get are both shown under the player before you tap Increase FPS.

faq.q: How long does it take to process?
faq.a: It depends on the video's resolution, how many frames it contains and how powerful your device is — every generated frame is real work. If a clip is large, the fast model in Settings gets through it three to five times quicker.

faq.q: Why did my video stop processing?
faq.a: Almost always because the app went to the background. Keep UScale in the foreground while it works, and leave the phone on a charger for long clips so it does not run flat mid-pass.

faq.q: Does slow motion processing happen in the cloud?
faq.a: No. Frame interpolation runs on your device, which is why it works with no signal and why your footage is never uploaded.

brighten-dark-photos.card_title: How to brighten a dark photo
brighten-dark-photos.card_desc: Recover underexposed night, concert and indoor shots.
brighten-dark-photos.title: How to Brighten a Dark Photo on iPhone Without Ruining It
brighten-dark-photos.description: Fix underexposed iPhone photos. Why raising exposure adds noise, what AI brightening does differently, and how to rescue a dark photo in UScale in one tap.
brighten-dark-photos.h1: How to brighten a dark photo on iPhone without ruining it
brighten-dark-photos.answer: To brighten a dark photo on iPhone, open UScale, tap Upscale your media → Photos and pick the underexposed shot. Choose Enlighten and tap Upscale — there is nothing to configure. The pass runs on your iPhone and saves the brightened photo as a new copy.
brighten-dark-photos.supply: An underexposed photo in your library
brighten-dark-photos.intro: Raising exposure in a normal editor multiplies the shadows and their noise equally, which is why a rescued night photo comes out grainy and desaturated. Enlighten lifts and denoises in the same pass, on your iPhone, with nothing to set.
brighten-dark-photos.why_h: Why dark photos fall apart when you brighten them
brighten-dark-photos.why_p: How much comes back depends on what is still left in the shadows.
why_list: Shadows carry the worst signal-to-noise ratio in the frame, so lifting them turns noise into visible blotches.
Colour goes first — deep shadows lose saturation before they lose detail.
Phone HDR already lifted the shadows once, so there is less headroom than the photo suggests.
Pure black holds no data at all. Very dark is fixable; black is not.
brighten-dark-photos.steps_h: Brighten a dark photo in UScale, step by step
brighten-dark-photos.steps_intro: Two taps once the photo is picked.

steps.p: Pick the original from the camera roll — a screenshot or a re-shared copy has already thrown away the shadow detail. Several photos can go in one batch.
It lifts the shadows, brings colour back into them and denoises in the same pass. There are no options: the model decides how far to lift each area.

It runs on your iPhone, works in airplane mode and uploads nothing. A very large photo is scaled down slightly first so it fits into one on-device pass, so the result can come back a little smaller than the original.
Check faces and the darkest corners before saving. The brightened photo is saved as a new copy and the original stays untouched.

brighten-dark-photos.img_alt: A dark concert photo brightened with AI in UScale on iPhone, shadows recovered
brighten-dark-photos.img_caption: A very dark concert photo with shadow detail and colour recovered.
tips: Shoot in RAW or ProRAW when you can — far more shadow information survives for the model to work with.
Need the resolution back after the resize? Run the brightened copy through Regular Upscale 2x or 4x.
Do not run Enlighten twice. The second pass mostly amplifies what the first one invented.
Dark and blurry? Brighten first, then unblur — denoising a lifted image beats lifting a sharpened one.
brighten-dark-photos.cta_p: AI brightening and denoising in one tap, running on your iPhone — two free photos a day.

faq.q: Why does the Photos app exposure slider make my photo look worse?
faq.a: It multiplies everything in the shadows, sensor noise included, with no idea what the scene should look like. Enlighten brightens and denoises together.

faq.q: Why did my brightened photo come back slightly smaller?
faq.a: A very large image is scaled down a little so it fits into what your iPhone can process in one pass. Run the result through Regular Upscale 2x or 4x to get the pixels back.

faq.q: Does UScale upload my dark photos to brighten them?
faq.a: No. Enlighten is an on-device mode: it works in airplane mode, needs no account and the photo never leaves your iPhone.

faq.q: Does brightening change the colours?
faq.a: It restores them. Deep shadows lose saturation first, so the pass usually brings colour back to something close to what you saw at the time.

film-negative-to-photo.card_title: How to turn film negatives into photos
film-negative-to-photo.card_desc: Digitise and invert 35mm negatives with your phone.
film-negative-to-photo.title: How to Convert Film Negatives to Photos with Your Phone
film-negative-to-photo.description: Turn 35mm film negatives into photos with your iPhone: how to light and photograph a strip, then invert and restore it with the Negative option.
film-negative-to-photo.h1: How to turn film negatives into photos
film-negative-to-photo.answer: To convert a film negative into a photo, photograph it on an even white light source, then open UScale, tap Upscale your media → Photos and choose Photo restoration. Turn on Negative in Advanced options, pick a mode and tap Upscale. About 40 seconds later the frame comes back inverted, colour-corrected and cleaned up.
film-negative-to-photo.supply: A 35mm negative strip and a bright, even light source
film-negative-to-photo.intro: A drawer of negatives is often the highest-quality version of a family archive that still exists — negatives hold more detail than the small prints made from them. The obstacle is simply that they are hard to look at. Your phone plus a white screen solves that in about two minutes per frame, and the Negative switch inside Photo restoration handles the part that trips most people up: inverting the image without ending up with a cyan, lifeless picture.
film-negative-to-photo.why_h: What makes a negative hard to digitise
film-negative-to-photo.why_p: Several things go wrong before software gets involved, and each has a simple fix.
why_list: The orange base — colour negative film has a built-in mask that must be neutralised, or a straight inversion comes out cyan and flat.
Uneven backlight — a bare lamp behind the film creates a hotspot; you need a diffused, even source instead.
Reflections — anything shiny in front of the film shows up in the capture, including your own phone.
Dust — negatives attract it, and every speck becomes a visible white dot after inversion.
Curl and age — film rolled up for decades will not sit flat, and colour negatives fade and shift just as prints do.
film-negative-to-photo.steps_h: Digitise a negative in UScale, step by step
film-negative-to-photo.steps_intro: A tablet or laptop showing a plain white screen makes an excellent light table.

steps.p: Open a plain white image full-screen on a tablet or laptop at maximum brightness. Lay a sheet of white paper over it to diffuse the pixels, then place the negative on top.
Hold the phone parallel to the film and fill the frame with a single negative. Tap to focus on the film itself, keep the room dim, and check that no lamp behind you reflects off the surface.

steps.h: Open Upscale your media → Photos and choose Photo restoration
steps.p: Select your captures — a whole strip photographed frame by frame can go in as one batch. Photo restoration is the mode that carries the negative tooling, and it runs on our servers.

steps.h: Turn on Negative in Advanced options
steps.p: It inverts the image and normalises the colours before restoration runs, which is what neutralises the orange mask rather than merely flipping it to cyan.

steps.h: Pick a mode for the restoration pass
steps.p: Enhanced Colorize for a colour negative, or when a black-and-white negative should end up in colour. Restore for a black-and-white negative that should stay monochrome.

steps.h: Tap Upscale, then save the positive
steps.p: About 40 seconds later the inverted, corrected and cleaned frame comes back as a positive photo. Zoom in to check the grain and the faces, then save it — and keep the raw negative capture as your digital master.

film-negative-to-photo.modes_h: Which mode to run after the inversion
film-negative-to-photo.modes_intro: Negative only handles the inversion. The mode decides what happens to the picture underneath — these are the app's previews.

modes.img_alt: Enhanced Colorize mode preview in UScale — the same portrait colorized with sharper detail
modes.sub: Restore and colorize with improved sharpness
modes.p: The right default for a faded colour negative, where the dyes have shifted so far that the colour has to be rebuilt. It also colourises black-and-white film.

modes.img_alt: Restore & Colorize mode preview in UScale — the same old portrait repaired and colorized
modes.p: Repair and colour without the extra sharpening — a safer choice on grainy 35mm, where Enhanced Colorize can turn grain into invented detail.

modes.img_alt: Restore mode preview in UScale — an old portrait cleaned up and left in black and white
modes.sub: Remove scratches while keeping the original colors
modes.p: Cleans dust and scratches and leaves the tones alone: for black-and-white negatives, and for colour film that held its colour.

modes.img_alt: Advanced Fix mode preview in UScale — a cracked, stained print of the kind this mode is built for
modes.sub: Fixes severe damage and boosts quality
modes.p: For film that is scratched, mouldy or physically damaged. It rebuilds heavily and drifts furthest from what was on the frame.

film-negative-to-photo.options_h: Advanced options that matter for negatives
film-negative-to-photo.options_intro: Negative is the one you cannot skip. The other two are worth knowing once your first frame looks right.

options.sub: Invert and normalize photo colors before restoration
options.p: The switch that does the conversion: it inverts the frame and neutralises the orange mask before restoration. Without it you get a cyan negative of a negative.

options.sub: Generates the result at a higher resolution
options.p: Negatives hold a lot of detail, so the higher-resolution models pay off here — especially for printing. Test one frame before committing a strip.

options.sub: Add eye color, clothing color, or other important details
options.p: Useful on a second pass: once you can read the scene, “blue car, green lawn, blonde hair” lands closer to the real day. Not used by Advanced Fix.

tips: Use a blower or a soft brush on the negative first — removing dust physically is much easier than removing it digitally.
Weigh curled film flat under a piece of clean glass; a picture frame pane works well.
Keep the room dim. Ambient light bouncing off the film surface is the biggest cause of washed-out negative scans.
Black-and-white negatives are easier than colour ones because there is no orange mask to neutralise. Start with those.
Test your setup on one frame before photographing a whole strip, and shoot frame by frame — one negative filling the phone frame gives far more pixels than six sharing it.
film-negative-to-photo.cta_p: Invert, restore and upscale film negatives on your iPhone. Restoration runs on our cloud models as part of Premium, starting with a {trial_days}-day free trial.

faq.q: Do I need a dedicated film scanner?
faq.a: For an archive project a film scanner gives the highest quality. For getting a drawer of negatives visible and shareable, a phone camera over a white screen is dramatically faster and the results are genuinely good.

faq.q: Why does my inverted negative look blue or cyan?
faq.a: That is the orange film mask still in play. Inverting the colours is not enough — the mask has to be neutralised, which is what the Negative option does before the restoration pass runs.

faq.q: Can I do this with slides as well?
faq.a: Slides are already positive, so leave Negative switched off. Photograph them on the same light table and run Photo restoration normally to clean up dust and fading.

faq.q: Which mode should I use on a black and white negative?
faq.a: Restore if it should stay black and white, Enhanced Colorize if you want it in colour. Both handle the dust and scratches; only the colour differs.

faq.q: Can I convert a whole roll at once?
faq.a: Photograph each frame separately, then select all the captures together in Photos — one batch shares the same mode and options, so you set them once and wait once.

fix-blurry-faces.card_title: How to fix blurry faces in photos
fix-blurry-faces.card_desc: Restore eyes, skin and hair in portraits and group shots.
fix-blurry-faces.title: How to Fix Blurry Faces in Photos (AI Face Restore)
fix-blurry-faces.description: Fix blurry faces in group photos with AI face restoration. When to use Face Enhancer, when Creative Upscale works better, and how to do it in UScale.
fix-blurry-faces.h1: How to fix blurry faces in photos
fix-blurry-faces.answer: To fix a blurry face, open UScale, tap Upscale your media → Photos and run Face Enhancer: a dedicated model rebuilds eyes, skin and hair on your device, and afterwards you choose which detected faces keep the enhancement. For large, close-up faces, Creative Upscale gives a better result.
fix-blurry-faces.supply: A photo with soft or small faces
fix-blurry-faces.intro: Faces are the reason general upscaling often disappoints. A group photo can be sharp overall while each face occupies a couple of hundred pixels — far too few for a general model to treat as more than a smudge. Face Enhancer knows the structure of a face and can rebuild eyes, lips and hair from very little. Its blind spot is the opposite case: trained on small, blurry faces, it adds less than you would expect to a large close-up, and that is where Creative Upscale takes over.
fix-blurry-faces.why_h: Why faces need their own model
fix-blurry-faces.why_p: The problem is not sharpness in general, it is how little of the frame a face usually occupies.
why_list: In a group photo, each face may be one or two percent of the total pixels.
General upscalers optimise for the whole image, so they average small faces into smooth blobs.
Eyes carry most of the perceived sharpness of a portrait — get them right and the whole face reads as sharp.
Skin texture is what separates a restored face from a plastic one, and crude sharpening destroys it first.
Face Enhancer was trained on small and blurry faces, which is why it adds so little to a big, already-detailed close-up. Use Creative Upscale for those.
fix-blurry-faces.steps_h: Restore faces in UScale, step by step
fix-blurry-faces.steps_intro: Two modes, and which one you want depends on how big the faces are in the frame.

steps.p: Tap Upscale your media, choose Photos and select the shot — or several at once. Use the original file rather than a shared or screenshotted copy, since faces suffer most from re-compression.
Face Enhancer runs entirely on your iPhone, so the photo is never uploaded. It detects every face in the frame and applies a dedicated restoration model to each one.

steps.h: Pick a style — Natural or Smoothed
steps.p: Natural keeps real skin texture and is the safer choice for portraits. Smoothed gives a cleaner face with harder edges, which helps when the source is very noisy.

steps.h: Tap Upscale and check each face
steps.p: Processing takes seconds. Pinch to zoom into each person: restoration happens face by face, so one can come out perfectly while another, further away, does not.

steps.h: Choose which faces keep the enhancement
steps.p: After processing you select the faces the enhancement applies to. A heavily blurred face in the background sometimes gets rebuilt into something strange, and switching it off — or switching on one the app skipped — tells the algorithm where to work.

steps.h: Big face in the frame? Run Creative Upscale instead
steps.p: For a close-up where the face already fills the picture, Creative Upscale usually wins: it rebuilds pores, hair and skin texture and returns a 2K, 4K or 8K result in about 30 seconds, processed in the cloud. Save whichever version you prefer as a new copy.

tips: Compare against the original at full zoom before saving. Face restoration is interpretation, and a strong result can subtly change how someone looks.
If only one person matters, crop to them — but if that makes the face fill the frame, switch to Creative Upscale.
Use the face selection after processing. Leaving a barely visible background face enhanced is the most common way a group photo ends up looking odd.
Faces in profile or partly hidden restore less reliably, and motion blur across a face is the one case no mode fully fixes yet.
Face Enhancer uploads nothing and needs no connection, so it is the mode for photos of children.
If neither mode gets you there, email the photo to alexandr.graschenkov91@gmail.com — the developer answers personally.
fix-blurry-faces.cta_p: Dedicated AI face restoration, running on your iPhone. Two free photos every day.

faq.q: Should I use Face Enhancer or Creative Upscale?
faq.a: Face Enhancer for small or soft faces — group shots, distant subjects, old scans — and it runs on your device. Creative Upscale for close-up portraits where the face is already large: it rebuilds pores and skin texture, which the face model largely leaves alone.

faq.q: Will face restoration change what someone looks like?
faq.a: Mildly, yes — the model reconstructs detail rather than recovering it exactly. On moderately soft faces the result stays very close to the person; on extremely small or smeared faces it can drift, so always compare before saving.

faq.q: Does it work on multiple faces in one photo?
faq.a: Yes. Each detected face is processed individually, and afterwards you choose which of them keep the enhancement — useful when a blurry background face comes out worse than it went in.

faq.q: Does it work on old scanned photos?
faq.a: Yes, and it is one of the most striking uses. Run the restoration pass first to remove scratches, then Face Enhancer on the result.

upscale-anime-art.card_title: How to upscale anime art and drawings
upscale-anime-art.card_desc: Enlarge illustrations and pixel art without mush.
upscale-anime-art.title: How to Upscale Anime Art and Drawings on iPhone
upscale-anime-art.description: Upscale anime art, illustrations and pixel art on iPhone without turning lines into mush. How AI upscaling handles flat colour and line art, step by step in UScale.
upscale-anime-art.h1: How to upscale anime art and drawings
upscale-anime-art.answer: To upscale anime art or a drawing, open it in UScale and run the 2x or 4x model. AI upscaling keeps line art crisp and flat colour clean instead of blurring edges the way a normal resize does, so a small illustration becomes a wallpaper- or print-sized file.
upscale-anime-art.supply: An illustration, anime frame or pixel-art image
upscale-anime-art.intro: Illustration is the friendliest possible input for an AI upscaler. Photographs are full of noise, texture and depth-of-field; drawings are made of clean lines and flat regions, which are exactly the structures these models predict most confidently. That is why a 4x upscale of a small anime image often looks like it was drawn at that size.
upscale-anime-art.why_h: Why drawings upscale better than photos
upscale-anime-art.why_p: The structure of illustration plays to every strength of a neural upscaler.
why_list: Line art is high-contrast and continuous, so the model can extend edges with confidence.
Flat colour fields have no texture to invent — they simply need clean boundaries.
There is no sensor noise or motion blur competing with the real detail.
Pixel art has perfectly predictable structure, which upscales into crisp shapes rather than soft blocks.
Compression artefacts around lines, common in images saved from the web, are cleaned up in the same pass.
upscale-anime-art.steps_h: Upscale artwork in UScale, step by step
upscale-anime-art.steps_intro: The same enhance flow as photos, with one setting worth changing.

steps.p: Save the image to your library and open it in UScale. Use the largest version you have — a thumbnail will always limit the outcome.
The face model is trained on photographic faces. On a drawn character it can push features towards photorealism, which is rarely what you want.
Illustration handles aggressive upscaling far better than photography does. 4x on a 1000-pixel image gives you a 4000-pixel file suitable for a poster or a desktop wallpaper.

steps.h: Check the lines at full zoom
steps.p: Zoom in on line intersections and hair. Clean, continuous lines mean the model handled it well; wobbling or doubled lines mean the source was too small.
Save the upscaled file to your library. It is now large enough for wallpaper, printing or use as a high-resolution asset.

upscale-anime-art.tips_h: Tips for artwork and pixel art
tips: Upscale before you add text or a watermark. Running the model over text produces subtly warped letterforms.
For true pixel art where you want to keep the blocky look, a nearest-neighbour resize is the right tool — AI upscaling deliberately smooths those hard edges.
Screenshots of video frames upscale well, but interlacing lines from old sources should be cleaned with the video enhance pass first.
If you are upscaling a whole set, use batch processing — artwork rarely needs per-image tuning.
upscale-anime-art.cta_p: 2x and 4x AI upscaling for illustrations, anime and pixel art, right on your iPhone.

faq.q: Is this a waifu2x alternative for iPhone?
faq.a: It solves the same problem — enlarging anime-style art without softening the lines — with a modern model that runs on your device instead of a website, and it handles photographs and video as well.

faq.q: Can I upscale a video of anime, not just a still?
faq.a: Yes. The video enhance pass applies the same model frame by frame, which works particularly well on animation because of the flat colour regions.

faq.q: Will upscaling change the art style?
faq.a: The 2x and 4x models preserve the original style and just add resolution. Creative Upscale is the one that reinterprets detail, so avoid it if faithfulness matters.
